rule.description: A backend contract flips any declared interface with at least 6 callable members into a fat seam when at least 2 of those members are never accessed through any receiver typed as the contract or one of its subtypes, or when at least 2 consumer functions use the contract and none of them uses its full surface. Every partial consumer function and every implementor class carrying call-path-free capabilities is reported.

checks.description: The backend contract declares so many capabilities that some of its members are never accessed through any receiver typed as the contract or one of its subtypes; every consumer and implementor still has to accept them.
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Interface segregation is violated when an interface forces holders to accept members they do not need; members with no call path behind the contract are the obligations nobody wanted.

matches.evidence: Node.js backend contract declares 12 callable members; only 7 are ever accessed through a receiver typed as the contract or a subtype. decodeImage, proportionalSize, resolveUri, fetchResponse and fetchResourceUrl are never called behind the seam.
Browser backend contract declares 10 callable members; only 7 are ever accessed through the contract. decodeImage, bitmapToData and fetchResourceUrl have no call path behind the seam.

checks.description: Consumer functions obtain backend capabilities through the fat contract but each one uses only a small disjoint slice of it; no consumer uses anywhere near the full surface.
checks.detected_relation: consumer function -> fat contract (strictly partial use)
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Each consumer is forced to depend on the whole capability surface to reach the part it needs, the dependency-pressure form of the same relation.

matches.evidence: Model initialization uses 2 of the 12 contract members (chunked blob fetch, session creation).
Inference pass uses 4 of the 12 contract members (resize, layout conversion, session run, float conversion).
Public background removal uses 1 of the 12 contract members (image encoding).
Public foreground removal uses 1 of the 12 contract members (image encoding).
Public segmentation masking uses 1 of the 12 contract members (image encoding).
Mask application uses 2 of the 12 contract members (mask resize, image encoding).
Browser model initialization uses 2 of the 10 contract members (chunked blob fetch, session creation).
Browser inference pass uses 4 of the 10 contract members (two resize operations, layout conversion, session run, float conversion).
Browser background removal uses 1 of the 10 contract members (image encoding).
Browser foreground removal uses 1 of the 10 contract members (image encoding).
Browser segmentation masking uses 1 of the 10 contract members (image encoding).
Browser mask application uses 2 of the 10 contract members (mask resize, image encoding).

checks.description: Classes implementing the backend contract provide or inherit members that exist only to satisfy the contract: no execution path reaches them through the seam.
checks.detected_relation: implementor class -> contract obligations without a call path
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The implementor side of the same relation: implementors are compelled to carry capabilities they never execute, including abstract base-class members forced onto every runtime flavour.

matches.evidence: Abstract Node.js plumbing class carries 5 contract capabilities with no call path through the contract: an abstract decodeImage member plus proportionalSize, resolveUri, fetchResponse and fetchResourceUrl delegations.
Concrete sharp backend implements decodeImage and inherits the never-called plumbing delegations, so it carries all 5 call-path-free capabilities.
Abstract browser plumbing class carries 3 contract capabilities with no call path through the contract: an abstract decodeImage member plus bitmapToData and fetchResourceUrl delegations.
Concrete canvas backend implements decodeImage and inherits the never-called bitmap and resource delegations, carrying all 3 call-path-free capabilities.

excluded.reason: single-member ambient interface, far below the 6-member contract threshold
configuration object with defaults, data rather than obligation-bearing callable members
type re-exports, not capability contracts; the rule counts callable member signatures only
small cohesive value class with no wide-contract relation

excluded.target: worker-proxy session handle ({base: unknown}) in packages/web/src/inference.ts
excluded.reason: opaque cross-worker serialization surface; the rule requires a declared interface contract, not an inline object type
